Broken or Damaged Tooth? When Might You Need a Same-Day Crown?

A cracked or broken tooth can happen suddenly, sometimes from biting something hard or because an old filling has weakened the tooth.

In many cases, the tooth may still be restored with a crown instead of being removed.

A same-day crown may be considered if:

• Part of the tooth has broken off
• A large filling has weakened the tooth
• The tooth is cracked or badly worn
• The tooth needs extra protection after treatment

If enough healthy tooth structure remains, your dentist may be able to design and place the crown during the same visit.

Not every damaged tooth is suitable for a same-day crown, so an examination is important before treatment is recommended.

Contact our dental team to have your tooth checked and discuss whether a same-day crown may be right for you.

Dental bonding vs veneers: which option is right for your smile?

Both treatments can improve the look of chipped, stained, uneven, or slightly gapped teeth, but they are not the same. Dental bonding is often used for smaller cosmetic fixes, while veneers may be recommended for a more complete smile transformation.

Dental bonding may help with:

• Small chips or cracks
• Minor gaps between teeth
• Slight tooth reshaping
• Small areas of discoloration
• A more conservative cosmetic option

Veneers may help with:

• Multiple visible smile concerns
• Stubborn stains that do not respond to whitening
• Worn, uneven, or misshapen teeth
• A longer-lasting smile makeover option
• A more uniform smile appearance

The right choice depends on your tooth condition, smile goals, budget, and oral health. A dental evaluation can help you compare both options and choose the treatment that fits your smile best.

Schedule your cosmetic dentistry consultation today.

Can Invisalign fix crowded or crooked teeth in adults?

Yes, Invisalign may help many adults improve mild to moderate crowding, crooked teeth, gaps, and alignment concerns without traditional metal braces. These clear aligners are removable, discreet, and designed to gradually move teeth into better positions.

Invisalign may be a good option if you have:

• Crowded front teeth
• Crooked or overlapping teeth
• Small gaps between teeth
• Teeth that shifted after braces
• Mild bite alignment concerns
• A desire for a more discreet orthodontic option

However, not every case is the same. Severe crowding, complex bite problems, or gum health concerns may require a different treatment plan. A dental evaluation can help determine whether Invisalign is suitable for your smile goals.

Our El Paso dental team can examine your teeth, review your bite, and explain your clear aligner options.

Schedule your Invisalign consultation today.

Waking Up With Jaw Pain or Headaches? Could Teeth Grinding Be the Cause?

Many people clench or grind their teeth at night without knowing it. 
Over time, this pressure can affect your teeth, jaw muscles, and bite.

Common signs of teeth grinding may include:

• Morning jaw pain or tightness
• Frequent headaches
• Tooth sensitivity
• Worn, chipped, or cracked teeth
• Sore facial muscles
• Pain when chewing
• Clicking or discomfort in the jaw

A custom nightguard may help protect your teeth from grinding damage and reduce pressure on the jaw while you sleep. Your dentist can check for signs of bruxism and recommend the right option based on your symptoms.

Do not ignore ongoing jaw pain or morning headaches. Early care can help protect your smile and prevent further tooth damage.

ownerUpdates.text: Snoring, waking up tired, morning headaches, or that afternoon brain fog that coffee can't fix? Your airway may be part of the story. At Strobel Dentistry in downtown Chicago, our airway dentistry program starts with a complimentary consultation and a close look at your anatomy using CBCT 3D imaging. If we suspect obstructive sleep apnea, we send you home with an easy at-home sleep test, so there's no overnight stay in a lab. When sleep apnea is confirmed, we walk you through personalized options, including a custom mandibular advancement device that gently positions your jaw forward to keep your airway open while you sleep. It's a comfortable, non-CPAP alternative for qualified patients, and for more complex cases we coordinate with sleep physicians. Better sleep can change how you feel all day, from energy and focus to mood. If you or a partner has noticed gasping, loud snoring, or restless nights, it's worth a conversation. Invisalign uses a series of custom-made, removable clear aligners to gradually shift your teeth into alignment. No wires, no brackets, and no food restrictions. For most patients, no one even notices they’re in treatment.

Downtown Chicago Invisalign at Strobel Dentistry is handled entirely in-house by certified providers, from free consultation to retainers at the end.

Guided Biofilm Therapy (GBT) changes the order of operations on a dental cleaning. Instead of opening with hand instruments and gritty polishing paste, we start by showing you where the problem actually is. A harmless dye makes biofilm visible on your teeth — that’s the soft bacterial layer behind most cavities and gum disease — so nothing gets missed and nothing gets scraped that didn’t need it.

From there, the AIRFLOW® Prophylaxis Master delivers a warm spray of air, water, and fine powder that lifts biofilm and stains off enamel, gumlines, implants, and orthodontics. Ultrasonic scaling handles any hardened tartar left behind. Strobel Dentistry is a GBT Certified practice, so our hygienists are trained in the full protocol and follow it the same way every visit.

A dental crown is a custom cap that restores a damaged, cracked, or heavily filled tooth, bringing back its strength, shape, and function. The old way meant two appointments spread weeks apart, with a temporary crown in between. 

Our Downtown Chicago same-day crowns change that entirely.
Using CEREC digital technology, our dentists design, mill, and place a permanent crown in a single visit. Say goodbye to temporary restorations and multiple appointments.

We use OralID, a light-based screening device, to check for oral tissue changes that can be easy to miss during a standard visual exam. It’s quick, comfortable, and can be added to routine cleanings and exams.

Strobel Dentistry is Now Offering Enhanced Oral Cancer Screenings!
